main_prompt: I have a reference trajectory and a real pneumatic robot controlled by a fixed MPC. The completed-lap JSON contains reference and real pose and velocity, u_mpc, compensation_mv, total_u_mv, six measured pressures, lock state, per-axis metrics, design memory, phase samples, and a 20 Hz trace. Coordinates are [GUI X, GUI Y, GUI phi]. Channels are [V0, V1, V2, V3, V4, V5]. Design one reusable pressure-aware hierarchical residual controller as a Python class named Compensator. Do not change the MPC, robot model, 100 ms lock planner, controller runtime, or external safety layer.

ARCHITECTURE: This is the advanced design path, not the simple matrix-PID path. The fixed MPC remains the base motion controller. The generated class may choose a P, PI, PD, PID, filtered acceleration-error, pressure-dominant, or hybrid motion residual according to measured evidence; it must not assume that PD or any other fixed combination is mandatory. Every unsupported term must be exactly zero. It may add deterministic motion-phase or direction scheduling when the data supports different rise, hold, reversal, and return behavior. In addition, every enabled channel must use a six-channel measured-pressure feedback layer around a physically meaningful pressure target. The pressure input must materially participate in compute. Do not return a controller that merely changes Kp and Kd while ignoring pressure.

ACTUATION SEMANTICS: The class returns signed requested_compensation, not a physical negative pressure or a final valve voltage. External actuation is preprojected_u = clip(u_mpc + requested_compensation, 0, u_max); total_u = antagonist_project(preprojected_u); applied_compensation = total_u - u_mpc. Every final valve voltage and pressure is nonnegative. A negative residual may only unload an existing positive u_mpc command. Always distinguish motion residual, pressure correction, signed requested compensation, applied compensation, and final total_u.

REFERENCE AXIS SELECTION: Compute reference peak-to-peak motion for X, Y, and phi. Select at most the two largest axes whose reference peak-to-peak motion exceeds 1.0 degree, and keep that selected set fixed for the task. Judge the selected axes independently using a 4.0 degree RMSE threshold, equivalent to 16.0 deg^2 MSE. An unselected axis has zero learned motion terms. If one selected axis is already accurate and smooth, its learned terms may remain zero while the other selected axis is compensated.

DIRECTION AND CHANNEL OWNERSHIP: Positive and negative physical valve commands are both nonnegative; direction is represented by choosing the active antagonist channel, not by commanding negative pressure. Use the commanded trajectory phase or persistent reference-motion direction, never noisy instantaneous tracking-error sign, to establish channel ownership. The fixed mapping is Y+ -> V0, Y- -> V1, phi+ -> V2, phi- -> V3, X+ -> V5, X- -> V4. During Y+, V1 may not receive positive learned drive; during Y-, V0 may not receive positive learned drive, and likewise for the other pairs. The inactive old side may receive a bounded negative residual only to unload its existing u_mpc during break-before-make handoff. Hold phases retain the preceding commanded direction until a deterministic reversal is established.

PER-AXIS RESPONSE METRICS: For each selected axis separately evaluate delay time, rising time, overshoot, steady-state error, and whole-lap MSE. Use them to identify late onset, slow rise, excessive peak, persistent final bias, reversal error, and overall tracking error. Do not collapse the axes into one aggregate score and do not require all five metrics to improve simultaneously. Never obtain lower MSE by creating materially worse overshoot, oscillation, pressure instability, or steady-state error. Report only metrics supported by the completed-lap data.

MOTION LAYER: Define pose_error = reference_pose - pose and make velocity_error = reference_velocity - velocity available, but use only the features justified by the measured response. A filtered acceleration_error may be estimated from consecutive reference_velocity and velocity samples; do not differentiate raw angle measurements directly. The motion request may use any supported subset of global or deterministic phase-specific 6x3 Kp, Kd, Ki, and Ka matrices. Kd, Ki, and Ka may each be entirely zero. When a term is used, apply the corresponding bounded integral, derivative filtering, anti-windup, or bumpless phase transfer required for stable execution. Cross-axis matrix terms are allowed only when repeated measured evidence shows that an input on one physical channel predictably disturbs another selected axis; otherwise keep the matrices sparse.

PRESSURE TARGET LAYER: For each enabled and direction-owned channel form an absolute pressure target from the base MPC voltage plus the bounded motion residual. Use the nominal calibrated regulator conversion pressure_per_mv_kpa, initialized from 0.09 kPa/mV unless the completed-lap data supports a channel-specific value: pressure_target = clip(pressure_per_mv_kpa * clip(u_mpc + motion_request, 0, u_max), 0, pressure_target_limit_kpa). Do not reinterpret the 30 kPa unlock threshold as a pressure target or operating minimum. Disable pressure targets for unselected axes and for the inactive antagonist side.

PRESSURE INNER LAYER: Define pressure_error = pressure_target - measured_pressure for enabled, direction-owned, locked channels. Use six independent pressure Kp and Ki values with bounded pressure integrals and anti-windup. Pressure feedback should correct supply variation, regulator mismatch, and repeatable fill/vent lag without chasing sample noise. During a normal rise it may increase positive drive when measured pressure is below target; during overshoot, hold, reversal, or unloading it may apply a negative residual to reduce an existing base command. Reset the pressure integral when a channel unlocks or loses direction ownership. Do not use pressure derivative unless repeated clean data proves it is necessary.

PHYSICAL ORDER: Sanitize inputs and update bounded controller states; determine deterministic phase and direction ownership; calculate the motion residual; calculate absolute pressure targets; calculate pressure PI correction; combine motion and pressure terms; apply per-channel output_limit_mv; apply electrical headroom [-u_mpc, u_max-u_mpc]; apply the lock mask; then apply output_slew_mv_per_s. Unlocked channels return zero and reset their output and pressure-integral states. External final voltage clipping, final voltage slew guards, the 100 ms lock plan, the 30 kPa unlock decision, and antagonist projection remain authoritative.

OSCILLATION AND HANDOFF: Inspect consecutive pose, velocity, pressure, compensation_mv, total_u_mv, and lock samples. Treat repeated channel alternation, rapid pressure reversals, late positive drive after the reference begins slowing, or repeated overshoot as a failed design. Correct it through earlier unloading, more damping, lower pressure-integral action, smoother phase transfer, or asymmetric rise/return tuning. Never chase sample-to-sample lock ownership and never command both members of an antagonist pair positively in the same phase.

ITERATION: Read stable_compensator_after_audit, last_design, design_memory_last_5, slow_response_priority, recurrent_phase_error_hotspots, phase_samples, and the full trace. In later rounds compare the previous expected effect with the measured five response metrics for each selected axis. Preserve proven motion and pressure terms, identify whether the remaining problem is motion-layer timing, pressure-target mismatch, pressure-loop tuning, saturation, handoff, or a physical limit, and change only the supported layer and phase. Do not restart from zero when a stable advanced controller exists, and do not repeat a rolled-back design unchanged.

REAL-TIME OPERATOR FEEDBACK PRIORITY: Non-empty operator feedback appended after END COMPLETED-LAP JSON REPORT has highest priority after hard safety and physical feasibility. Apply it to the named axis, phase, channel, pressure behavior, or response metric. State exactly how the motion layer, pressure target, or pressure PI was changed in response. Do not merely acknowledge the feedback.

EXPLANATION CONTRACT: On the first design, failure_analysis is a short uncompensated-baseline diagnosis. On every later design, failure_analysis compares the previous expected effect with the new measured delay time, rising time, overshoot, steady-state error, and MSE for each selected axis and states which controller layer caused the miss. design_strategy states the concrete structural and numerical changes in the motion layer, phase scheduler, pressure target, and pressure PI. expected_effect states measurable predictions for the next real lap. Keep all explanations concise and axis-specific.
{round_instruction}
COMMON EXECUTION ERROR TO AVOID: Do not call self.reset() or any other self method from __init__ or compute. Initialize every state explicitly. Only the runtime calls reset().

SOURCE-CODE CONTRACT: Return exactly one loop-free Compensator class with only __init__(self), reset(self, feedback), and compute(self, u_mpc, pose, velocity, reference_pose, reference_velocity, pressure, lock_state, trajectory_time). The class must expose output_limit_mv (6,), output_slew_mv_per_s (6,), and u_max_mv. It should expose the motion matrices actually selected from Kp, Kd, Ki, and Ka (each 6x3 when present), plus pressure_kp_mv_per_kpa (6,), pressure_ki_mv_per_kpa_s (6,), pressure_integral_limit_kpa_s (6,), pressure_per_mv_kpa (6,), and pressure_target_limit_kpa (6,). Do not create nonzero Kd, Ki, or Ka merely to make the controller look complete. It may expose a small number of deterministic phase-specific matrices and thresholds. Set disabled axes and channels to zero. Keep source_code under 8000 characters and keep the state bounded. Do not use imports, files, network, processes, eval, exec, loops, recursion, comprehensions, exceptions, decorators, inheritance, helper methods, private attributes, or unbounded state. Allowed NumPy calls are array, asarray, zeros, ones, clip, sign, maximum, minimum, where, dot, matmul, mean, sum, and abs. Allowed built-ins are abs, min, max, float, int, len, and bool.

VALIDATED IMPLEMENTATION TEMPLATE: Use this executable structure and change its numeric arrays or add only compact deterministic phase selection. Do not call methods such as .copy(), .upper(), .astype(), or .tolist(), and do not add helper functions. Unsupported Kd, Ki, or Ka matrices remain zero.

class Compensator:
    def __init__(self):
        self.kp_matrix = np.zeros((6, 3))
        self.kd_matrix = np.zeros((6, 3))
        self.ki_matrix = np.zeros((6, 3))
        self.ka_matrix = np.zeros((6, 3))
        self.integral_limit_deg_s = np.zeros(3)
        self.pressure_kp_mv_per_kpa = np.zeros(6)
        self.pressure_ki_mv_per_kpa_s = np.zeros(6)
        self.pressure_integral_limit_kpa_s = np.zeros(6)
        self.pressure_per_mv_kpa = np.ones(6) * 0.09
        self.pressure_target_limit_kpa = np.ones(6) * 200.0
        self.enabled_channels = np.zeros(6)
        self.output_limit_mv = np.zeros(6)
        self.output_slew_mv_per_s = np.zeros(6)
        self.u_max_mv = 2500.0
        self.integral_error = np.zeros(3)
        self.pressure_integral = np.zeros(6)
        self.previous_velocity_error = np.zeros(3)
        self.filtered_acceleration_error = np.zeros(3)
        self.direction_memory = np.zeros(3)
        self.previous_output = np.zeros(6)
        self.last_time = 0.0

    def reset(self, feedback):
        self.integral_error = np.zeros(3)
        self.pressure_integral = np.zeros(6)
        self.previous_velocity_error = np.zeros(3)
        self.filtered_acceleration_error = np.zeros(3)
        self.direction_memory = np.zeros(3)
        self.previous_output = np.zeros(6)
        self.last_time = 0.0

    def compute(self, u_mpc, pose, velocity, reference_pose, reference_velocity, pressure, lock_state, trajectory_time):
        pose_value = np.asarray(pose)
        pose_value = np.where(pose_value == pose_value, np.clip(pose_value, -1000.0, 1000.0), 0.0)
        reference_value = np.asarray(reference_pose)
        reference_value = np.where(reference_value == reference_value, np.clip(reference_value, -1000.0, 1000.0), 0.0)
        velocity_value = np.asarray(velocity)
        velocity_value = np.where(velocity_value == velocity_value, np.clip(velocity_value, -1000.0, 1000.0), 0.0)
        reference_velocity_value = np.asarray(reference_velocity)
        reference_velocity_value = np.where(reference_velocity_value == reference_velocity_value, np.clip(reference_velocity_value, -1000.0, 1000.0), 0.0)
        pressure_value = np.asarray(pressure)
        pressure_value = np.where(pressure_value == pressure_value, np.clip(pressure_value, 0.0, 1000.0), 0.0)
        base_u = np.asarray(u_mpc)
        base_u = np.where(base_u == base_u, np.clip(base_u, 0.0, self.u_max_mv), 0.0)
        raw_time = np.asarray(trajectory_time)
        safe_time = np.where(raw_time == raw_time, np.clip(raw_time, 0.0, 1000000.0), self.last_time)
        current_time = float(safe_time)
        dt = min(0.05, max(0.0, current_time - self.last_time))
        self.last_time = current_time
        pose_error = reference_value - pose_value
        velocity_error = reference_velocity_value - velocity_value
        acceleration_error = np.zeros(3)
        if dt > 0.0:
            acceleration_error = (velocity_error - self.previous_velocity_error) / dt
        self.previous_velocity_error = velocity_error
        self.filtered_acceleration_error = 0.8 * self.filtered_acceleration_error + 0.2 * acceleration_error
        self.integral_error = np.clip(self.integral_error + pose_error * dt, -self.integral_limit_deg_s, self.integral_limit_deg_s)
        moving = np.abs(reference_velocity_value) > 0.02
        self.direction_memory = np.where(moving, np.sign(reference_velocity_value), self.direction_memory)
        ownership = np.array([float(self.direction_memory[1] > 0.0), float(self.direction_memory[1] < 0.0), float(self.direction_memory[2] > 0.0), float(self.direction_memory[2] < 0.0), float(self.direction_memory[0] < 0.0), float(self.direction_memory[0] > 0.0)])
        lock_mask = np.array([1.0 if lock_state[0] == 'L' else 0.0, 1.0 if lock_state[1] == 'L' else 0.0, 1.0 if lock_state[2] == 'L' else 0.0, 1.0 if lock_state[3] == 'L' else 0.0, 1.0 if lock_state[4] == 'L' else 0.0, 1.0 if lock_state[5] == 'L' else 0.0])
        motion_raw = np.matmul(self.kp_matrix, pose_error) + np.matmul(self.kd_matrix, velocity_error) + np.matmul(self.ki_matrix, self.integral_error) + np.matmul(self.ka_matrix, self.filtered_acceleration_error)
        motion_request = motion_raw * ownership * self.enabled_channels
        planned_u = np.clip(base_u + motion_request, 0.0, self.u_max_mv)
        pressure_target = np.clip(self.pressure_per_mv_kpa * planned_u, 0.0, self.pressure_target_limit_kpa) * ownership * self.enabled_channels
        pressure_error = (pressure_target - pressure_value) * ownership * self.enabled_channels * lock_mask
        pressure_state_mask = ownership * self.enabled_channels * lock_mask
        self.pressure_integral = np.clip((self.pressure_integral + pressure_error * dt) * pressure_state_mask, -self.pressure_integral_limit_kpa_s, self.pressure_integral_limit_kpa_s)
        pressure_correction = (self.pressure_kp_mv_per_kpa * pressure_error + self.pressure_ki_mv_per_kpa_s * self.pressure_integral) * pressure_state_mask
        inactive_unload = -base_u * self.enabled_channels * (1.0 - ownership)
        raw_output = motion_request + pressure_correction + inactive_unload
        amplitude_target = np.clip(raw_output, -self.output_limit_mv, self.output_limit_mv)
        headroom_target = np.clip(amplitude_target, -base_u, self.u_max_mv - base_u)
        self.previous_output = self.previous_output * lock_mask
        target = headroom_target * lock_mask
        maximum_step = self.output_slew_mv_per_s * dt
        output = self.previous_output + np.clip(target - self.previous_output, -maximum_step, maximum_step)
        self.previous_output = output
        return output

IMPLEMENTATION PIPELINE: In compute, sanitize all arrays; calculate dt no greater than 0.05 s; calculate pose_error and velocity_error; estimate and filter acceleration_error only from consecutive velocity signals; update bounded pose integrals; update persistent commanded-direction memory from reference_velocity; map direction memory to the fixed V0/V1, V2/V3, V5/V4 ownership; select global or deterministic phase-specific gains; calculate the motion residual; construct pressure_target from u_mpc plus motion residual; calculate measured pressure error and bounded pressure PI; combine the two layers; use output_limit_mv, electrical headroom, lock_state, and output_slew_mv_per_s in that order; store bounded prior state; return six finite signed requested-compensation values. reset must clear pose integral, pressure integral, direction memory, filters, timing, and previous output.

Before returning, report reference peak-to-peak motion, selected axes, and the five response metrics available for each selected axis. Identify one onset sample, one hold or overshoot sample, one reversal sample, and one near-zero-error sample. For each, distinguish u_mpc, motion residual, pressure target, measured pressure, pressure PI correction, requested compensation, applied compensation, and final total_u. Confirm channel ownership, lock masking, electrical headroom, and the maximum 50 ms output step.

OUTPUT: Return exactly one JSON object with schema=1, exact request_id={request_id}, exact task_hash={task_hash}, base_generation={base_generation}, created_by, rationale, design_strategy, expected_effect, failure_analysis, and source_code. Do not edit files or run the robot.
first_round: Treat the valid measured lap as the uncompensated baseline. Select at most two reference-motion axes, calculate their available five response metrics, and enable only axes whose RMSE exceeds 4.0 degrees or whose supported overshoot, delay, or steady-state evidence clearly requires correction. Build a conservative but nontrivial pressure-aware hierarchical controller: an enabled channel must use measured pressure in addition to motion error. Do not invent a prior advanced-controller result.
later_round: DESIGN STAGE: SECOND OR LATER ADVANCED ROUND.

Compare the last advanced controller's expected effect with the latest measured delay time, rising time, overshoot, steady-state error, and MSE for each selected axis. Diagnose whether each miss came from motion gains, phase timing, direction ownership, pressure-target construction, pressure PI, saturation, or physical limits. Change the responsible layer while preserving the parts that already improved measured behavior.
quality_above_30: The latest total MSE is {latest_mse:.6f} deg^2. This aggregate value signals poor overall tracking but does not authorize aggressive changes on every axis or layer. Use per-axis response metrics and phase/pressure evidence to locate the responsible layer.
quality_at_or_below_30: The latest total MSE is {latest_mse:.6f} deg^2. Preserve stable behavior and use per-axis response metrics to refine only the remaining motion phase or pressure-layer defect.
quality_unavailable: The latest total MSE is unavailable. Use only valid per-axis metrics, phase samples, pressure traces, and measured design history; do not claim improvement without valid evidence.
